children: SYDNEY--Australian business conditions in August turned negative for the first time in six years as firms worried about ongoing global shocks and falling profits.
Business confidence fell 2 points to minus-8 points in August and remained well below its long-run average, according to the National Australia Bank's latest business survey.
"Ongoing global uncertainty, volatility in oil prices and continued cost pressures appear to be weighing on business confidence," said Michael Hayes, an economist at NAB
Business conditions fell 5 points over the month to minus 1 point, the data showed.

The drop in business conditions and confidence traces a significant retreat in consumer confidence over the last few months, with households worried about the prospect of further interest rate increases.
The Reserve Bank of Australia has warned that inflation remains too high, with the bank's Governor Michele Bullock going so far as to say rate increases are "quite likely."
The RBA's policy-setting board meets at the end of the month amid forecasts from some economists that it could tighten another two times before the end of the year.
House prices have also been in sharp retreat since May, delivering a further hit to confidence.
The decline in business conditions in August was broad-based across industries and was driven by a 10-point fall in profitability and a 5-point fall in trading conditions, the survey showed.
Both subcomponents are now sitting at new post-Covid lows, the bank said.
The decline in the profitability index bears watching, given its leading relationship with broader labor market conditions, Hayes said.
Cost and price growth measures remained broadly unchanged in the month, staying elevated compared to their long-run averages, according to the report.
A spike in capacity utilization seen July partially unwound in August, declining 0.6 percentage points to 82.5% and remains around levels seen at the start of the year.
